summary: A very short note from 1971 that reserves one link number, 191, on the early ARPANET for network measurement work. The number was meant to be the highest unassigned link, but an earlier calculation of 223 had been wrong. Anyone wanting to use the link was asked to clear it first with the Liaison Officer at the Network Measurement Center.

plainLanguage.summary: Imagine a school hallway with numbered lockers. This note says one locker, number 191, is saved only for the people who measure how the hallway is working, and you must ask them before using it.

questions: which arpanet link was reserved for measurement
what was the network measurement center
subtitle: A one-paragraph note that sets aside link 191 on the early network for measurement work.

tldr.problem: The Network meeting at the University of Illinois agreed to reserve one link for measurements, and the number first worked out for it was wrong.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC corrects the number: the highest unassigned link is 191, not the 223 that was miscalculated, and link 191 is assigned for measurement use.
tldr.outcome: Anyone wanting to use the link has to clear it with the Liaison Officer at the Network Measurement Center (NMC).

today: The metadata gives this RFC an Unknown status and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is a short 1971 assignment note.

sections.title: A Link Set Aside for Measurement
sections.content:
At the Network meeting at the University of Illinois, it was agreed to reserve a link for use in measurements. The link chosen was the highest unassigned link.

The note is dated 25 February 1971 and comes from J. Postel and C. Crocker at UCLA Computer Science. It is a single paragraph with no protocol detail.
sections.plainLanguage: The grown-ups at a meeting agreed to save one numbered slot for measuring things. This note says which number.

sections.title: Correcting the Number
sections.content:
The link chosen was the highest unassigned link, which was incorrectly calculated to be number 223. The RFC states that the correct number is 191.

Therefore link 191 is assigned for measurement use. The RFC does not explain how the 223 figure was reached, only that it was wrong.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone did the counting wrong and said 223. The right answer is 191, so that is the locker that is saved.

sections.title: Getting Permission to Use It
sections.content: Use of this link should be cleared with the Liaison Officer at the Network Measurement Center (NMC). The note gives no other rules about what may be sent on the link or how.
sections.plainLanguage: If you want to use locker 191, you have to ask the person in charge of measuring first.
